story.title: The flood under the trees
story.lede: When Village Creek overflows, the water spreads beneath the hardwood canopy. From above it still looks like forest, but the radar hears the water.
body: NISAR's L-band waves are about 24 cm long, long enough to slip through the leaves. Over a flooded forest they hit the water, bounce off a trunk and come straight back. That double bounce makes HH jump several decibels while HV barely moves.

So flooded hectares leap sideways on the floor, into the double bounce corner, and return when the water drains. Open fields beside the river do the opposite: smooth water mirrors the pulse away and they vanish into the dark.

beats.caption: Before the storm: the bottomland forest sits with the pines.
The creek overflows. Flooded forest bounces right.
The water drains and the forest returns home.
A smaller September flood reaches only the lowest ground.
